matches.gold_text: Proposals must be submitted by 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025.
The program administrator(s) must develop the curriculum for and administer AI Prep for Track A and/or Track B; ESD will award up to two contracts.
For Track A, the administrator must develop a targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income students.
For Track A, the administrator must provide participant stipends and wrap-around supports including mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise.
The Track A curriculum should consist of online AI courses developed with input from leading researchers and industry experts, with mentorship opportunities and real-world machine learning projects.
For Track B, the administrator must deliver an industry-informed, comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment and connect them to AI jobs.
The Track B program should consist of online AI courses with curriculum that incorporates industry input on technical skills and learning milestones.
The program should serve a minimum of 250 participants, with priority given to applicants that serve more than 400 participants.
Over 50% of program participants should be low-income.
The majority of program graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.
Applicants must be organizations with a strong track record in workforce development in AI or similar fields.
If applicants form a team, one organization must be the lead for the proposed programming.

Applicants must have experience in at least three of four domains: academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training programs, serving low-income populations, and working in the New York market.
Proposed budgets may not exceed $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks over the total contract period, or they will not be considered.
The program operating period funded by ESD is up to 18 months.
Applicants must provide their own budget with associated justification.
Indirect costs are not allowable under this grant and must not be included in the budget.
The extent of any cost matching should be indicated in the budget template.
Awarded applicants must track and record information relevant to the success of the grant, with data points determined during contract negotiation.

The Technical Proposal must include a cover letter describing the organization's mission and history, annual budget, annual number of participants served, employer partnerships, and motivations for applying.
The proposal must describe any work the organization does to train a high-tech workforce in AI and related fields, excluding college students.
The proposal must include a monthly timeline for planning and administering the program through completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort.
The process and timeline should cover curriculum development, recruitment, training duration, cohort size, stipend and supports, and internship or job placement.
The proposal must describe how AI Prep funding will let the organization expand similar existing programming.
The proposal must include one-page resumes of key personnel who would administer the program.
The proposal must include letters from partner employers committing to provide paid internships or full-time employment to graduates.
The proposal must describe how the respondent would define low-income and target recruitment for the applicable Track(s).
The proposal must estimate annual performance on participants served, low-income completion percentage, and placement rate, justified by historical experience or partner commitments.
Respondents should provide a line-by-line price proposal of the proposed fees to accomplish the scope of work.
Respondents must include the Diversity Practices Questionnaire (Appendix B) in their response.
Technical Proposals should be organized with bookmarks matching the information requested in the listed outline.
Respondents should complete and submit the listed Administrative Proposal items in the order listed.
Proposals must be submitted only via the Dropbox upload; facsimile, hardcopy and email submissions will not be accepted.
Respondents must create a main folder named with the company name, RFP title and date of submission.
The main folder must contain two subfolders, one for the Administrative Proposal and one for the Technical Proposal.
Questions about the RFP must be submitted by email, citing the RFP page and section, by the question deadline.
Contractor staff assigned to the project are subject to ESD approval.
The contractor may not subcontract services beyond those indicated in its proposal without prior written approval of the State Project Manager.
ESD sets an overall 30 percent MWBE participation goal, and the contractor must document good faith efforts to use MWBE subcontractors and suppliers.
Respondents must submit an MWBE Utilization Plan with their proposal.
ESD sets an overall 6% SDVOB participation goal for the contract.
Respondents must submit a completed SDVOB Utilization Plan on Form OCSD-4 with the proposal.
The selected respondent must carry Commercial General Liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate.
The selected respondent must carry Sexual Abuse and Molestation insurance of $1 million.
ESD must be named as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on the Commercial General Liability and Auto Liability policies.
For Track A, the administrator must help students secure paid internships.
For Track A, the administrator must create a program application and evaluation process and conduct needs assessments to identify and address student barriers to success.
For Track A, the administrator should propose whether training runs during the academic year or as summer courses, aligned with employer internship hiring cycles.
For Track B, the training schedule should be immersive and deliverable part-time or full-time.
For Track B, the program should provide participant stipends and wrap-around supports, including success coach staff to address barriers to completion.
For Track B, the program should provide full-time job connection support in an AI-related field.
The administrator must cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers, to inform training content and to generate internship or employment opportunities.
Respondents applying for both tracks must describe their organizational capacity and strategy to manage two programs simultaneously.
If a vehicle is used in the business, the selected respondent must carry Commercial Automobile insurance with a limit of at least $1 million.

verdicts.text: Respondents are prohibited from contacting any New York State employee about this procurement other than the designated contacts (Julia Borukhov, Jordan Kaplan) during the restricted period, which lasts until approval of the Contract.
All contacts and inquiries regarding this procurement must be made by email to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.
Proposals must be submitted to the designated Dropbox at https://www.dropbox.com/request/AIPrep.
Proposals that arrive after the submission deadline of 2:00 PM ET on October 1, 2025 will not be accepted.
The contractor must develop the curriculum for and administer the AI Prep program for Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) and/or Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs).
Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) must provide low-income matriculating undergraduate students with AI training aimed at securing paid internship opportunities at leading tech companies.

Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs) must connect low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment to AI jobs through an accelerated training or bootcamp that serves as an alternative to traditional degree programs.
The program must serve New Yorkers who are currently underrepresented in the tech industry and who cannot reasonably access training on their own.
The administrator must develop and deliver a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income college students that includes paid internship placements.
The program must create direct pathways from education to the AI industry and help build a talent pipeline for AI employers.
The administrator must develop a targeted outreach and recruitment strategy for low-income students.
The administrator must create a program application and evaluation process.
The administrator must conduct needs assessments to identify and address student barriers to success.
The administrator must design an industry-informed AI curriculum.
The administrator must deliver and manage the AI training program.
The administrator must provide participant stipends and wrap-around supports including mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise.
The administrator must help students secure paid internships.
The administrator must cultivate and maintain relationships with leading industry employers to inform training content and generate paid internship opportunities.
The curriculum must consist of online AI courses developed with input from leading researchers and industry experts, with opportunities for mentorship and real-world machine learning projects.
The proposal must state whether the training program will be offered during the academic year or through summer courses, demonstrating alignment with employer internship hiring cycles and needs.
The training must be tailored to help students secure paid internship placements with leading New York State technology companies.
The internships must allow students to apply their newly acquired AI skills through real-world experience and networking, ultimately leading to full-time jobs.
The program must include a training schedule that is immersive and can be delivered part-time or full-time.
The program must include evaluation metrics to measure participant skill attainment during training.
The program must provide professional development support for trainees throughout training.
The program must state the credentials expected as a result of training completion, if applicable.
The program must provide full-time job connection support in an AI-related field.
The award is for an initial term of up to 18 months, with possible renewal or extension based on performance, need, and availability of funds.
An MWBE or SDVOB firm requesting inclusion on the subcontractor interest list must send its contact information and a copy of its NYS MWBE or SDVOB certification to AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov.
The proposed program should serve a minimum of 250 participants.
Priority is given to applicants that serve more than 400 participants.
Over 50% of program participants should be low-income.
The majority of program graduates should secure paid internships or full-time employment in artificial intelligence or a closely related field.
The applicant must be an organization with a strong track record for workforce development in AI or similar fields.
If applicants form a team, one organization must be designated as the lead for the proposed programming.
The applicant must be either a non-profit or a for-profit entity.

The applicant must have experience in at least three of the four listed domains (academic services to college students, high-tech accelerated training programs, serving low-income populations, working in the New York market) to qualify to administer the program.
Applicants must detail their own budget and provide an associated justification.
Proposed budgets must not exceed $2M for one track or $4M for both tracks for the total contract period, and budgets exceeding these amounts will not be considered.
Applicants should submit a proposed budget comprised of the specified cost information, mapped to the program duration.
The proposed budget must include staff salary and benefits costs.
The proposed budget must include wraparound supports and the proposed participant stipend level.
The proposed budget may include other costs deemed necessary for program success, including curriculum development and implementation, marketing, and events.
Indirect costs are not an allowable cost under this grant and must not be included in the budget.
The applicant must indicate the extent of any cost matching in the budget template.
Applicants may propose and offer justification for an alternative definition of the proposed eligibility definition (Pell Grant eligibility).
The awarded applicant must track and record information relevant to the success of the grant.
The awarded applicant must make the tracked data available to ESD upon request.
The data points captured and tracked must include, at minimum, the number of applicants and the percentage of those who are low-income.
The data points captured and tracked must include the number of participants who enroll and the percentage of those who are low-income.
The data points captured and tracked must include the number of participants who complete the program and the percentage of those who are low-income.
The data points captured and tracked must include the paid internship placement rate and the percentage of placements that are for low-income students.
The data points captured and tracked must include the full-time job placement rate and the percentage of placements that are for low-income individuals.
The data points captured and tracked must include the participating colleges and universities.
The data points captured and tracked must include the participating employer partners.
Questions about the RFP must be submitted by August 29, 2025.
The anticipated contract start date is January 1, 2026.
Interviews, if necessary, are anticipated to take place in the first week of November 2025.
The successful respondent is anticipated to be announced on November 14, 2025.

The Technical Proposal must include a cover letter describing the organization's mission and history, annual budget, annual number of participants served, employer partnerships, and motivations for applying to run AI Prep.
The Technical Proposal must describe how the organization delivers substantive, skill-based, college-level or accelerated immersive training in AI.
The Technical Proposal must identify the industry experts the organization partners with for its AI training.
The Technical Proposal must explain how the organization ensures its curriculum remains current and aligns with employer demand.

The Technical Proposal must describe the Respondent's work with college students, detailing length of training, number of students served, number of cohorts, cost per student, and internship and/or job placement rates of recent program graduates.

The Technical Proposal must describe the Respondent's work training a high-tech workforce in AI and related fields excluding college students, including length of training, number of participants served, number of cohorts, cost per participant, and job placement rate of recent program graduates.
The Technical Proposal must describe the Respondent's work with low-income students or individuals, including the number served and any additional supports provided.
The Technical Proposal must describe how the Respondent coordinates with individual employers to place participants in AI-related internships or jobs, if not already addressed.
The Technical Proposal must describe any work the Respondent does in the New York market, if not already addressed.
The Technical Proposal's Project Plan section must describe how the Respondent's organization would administer the AI Prep program.
The Project Plan must include a monthly timeline for planning and administering the program through the completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort.
The process and timeline must cover curriculum development, or specify that it is already completed.
The process and timeline must cover recruiting participants for Track A or Track B.
The proposal must state the proposed training duration.
The proposal must state the proposed cohort size.
The proposal must state the proposed stipend level and/or any other supports offered.
The process and timeline must cover internship or full-time job placement.
The proposal must describe how AI Prep funding will allow the Respondent to expand any similar programming it currently offers.
The proposal must detail how many additional participants the Respondent will be able to serve with the AI Prep funding.
The proposal must explain how the Respondent will maintain or enhance the quality of its current programming.

Respondents applying for both Tracks must provide a detailed description of their organizational capacity and strategy to manage two programs simultaneously in accordance with the expectations set forth in this RFP.
The proposal must include one-page resumes of key personnel who would be involved in administering the program.
The proposal must include letters from partner employers demonstrating their commitment to providing paid internships or full-time employment to graduates of the program.
The proposal must describe how the Respondent would define low-income for the purposes of this program and how it would target recruitment for the applicable Track(s).
The proposal must include details on any relevant partnerships the organization has with nonprofits and any New York colleges or universities.
The proposal must describe how the organization currently measures and reports the success of its program.

The proposal must estimate expected annual performance against the specified metrics (total participants served annually, percentage of low-income participants completing the curriculum, and paid internship or full-time job placement rate of graduates), justified by historical experience and/or commitments from proposed program partners.
The Technical Proposal must include a line-by-line price proposal of the proposed fees to accomplish the scope of work.

The price proposal must include Personnel Services (PS) costs broken out by job title, name of employee (if known), hourly rate or annual compensation rate, fringe rate, percentage of time dedicated to project, and cost to contract.
The proposal must include a line-by-line price proposal for Other Than Personnel Services (OTPS) costs, with each OTPS cost on a separate line showing cost to contract and number of each item.
Each Respondent must submit the Diversity Practices Questionnaire (Appendix B) with its RFP response so that ESD's Office of Contractor and Supplier Diversity can score Diversity Practices.
The Respondent should submit a proposal that clearly and concisely provides all of the information requested in the RFP.
The proposal should emphasize conformance to the RFP instructions and requirements as well as completeness and clarity of the response.
The Respondent must thoroughly read and follow all instructions contained in the RFP, and non-compliant proposals may be scored down or deemed nonresponsive.
The Technical Proposal must be organized with bookmarks identified to match the specific information requested in the RFP's technical information listing.
The Technical Proposal must contain a cover page including the Respondent's contact information.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Table of Contents.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Firm Experience and Qualifications section.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Staff Experience and Qualifications section.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Project Plan and Approach section.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Cost of Services section.
The Technical Proposal must contain a Diversity Practices Questionnaire.
Respondents must not include information in the Technical Proposal beyond what is specifically requested.
The successful Respondent must agree to abide by the standard requirements stated in Schedule A of this RFP and provide any information the Corporation requests in connection with those requirements.
Respondents must complete and submit the listed administrative items in the order in which they are listed.
The Administrative Proposal must include a Non-Collusive Bidding Certification.
The Administrative Proposal must include a Conflict of Interest Attestation.
The Administrative Proposal must include the State Finance Law §§139-j and 139-k forms.
The Administrative Proposal must include a Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire.
The Administrative Proposal must include an Iran Divestment Act Statement.
The Administrative Proposal must include an Executive Order 16 Certification.
The Administrative Proposal must include an Executive Order 177 Certification.

The Administrative Proposal must include the Non-Discrimination and Contractor & Supplier Diversity Requirements forms OCSD-1 (MWBE and SDVOB Participation / EEO Policy Statement), OCSD-2 (Staffing Plan) and OCSD-4 (MWBE and SDVOB Utilization Plan).
The Administrative Proposal must include a Certification under State Tax Law Section 5-a, Form ST-220-CA or the ST-220 affidavit.
The Administrative Proposal must include a W-9 Form.
By submitting a proposal, firms indicate their acceptance of the conditions in this RFP.
Proposals submitted in any manner other than as described in these instructions (e.g., facsimile, hardcopies, emails) will not be accepted.
The main submission folder must be named using the convention "company name – RFP title – date of Submission" (e.g., "ABDX, Inc. – AIPrepRFP – 08.08.2025").
The main folder must contain two subfolders, one for the Administrative Proposal and one for the Technical Proposal.
All documents in the submission folders must be clearly labeled.
Questions will not be accepted orally.
Respondents are strongly encouraged to review all posted questions and answers.
All costs associated with preparing and submitting a response to this RFP are borne solely by the Respondent.
By submitting a proposal, the respondent waives any and all claims against ESD relating to ESD's retention or use of the Response Information.

The awarded contract is not valid or enforceable, and the Corporation bears no liability under it, until the Office of the State Comptroller (OSC) has granted any required review and approval under Public Authorities Law §2879-a.
The Contractor must perform its services in accordance with applicable professional standards.
The Contractor must correct, at no charge to the Corporation, any services that fail to meet applicable professional standards and result in obvious or patent errors in the progression of its work.
The Contractor must assert any claim for price or time adjustment resulting from a Corporation-ordered change within 30 days of receiving the written notification of change.
The Contractor must continue performing the contract as modified and may not suspend work pending resolution of a change-related claim.

Changes or additions ordered by the Corporation are limited to work within the general scope of the contract and exclude professional services requiring licenses or specialized expertise such as engineering, architectural, environmental consulting, abatement, treatment and testing work.
Any equitable price adjustment for a change must be calculated using the billing rates set forth in the contract.
Contractor staff assigned to work on this project are subject to approval by the Corporation.
It is highly desirable that staff assigned to the project continue working on it until completion.
The Contractor should notify the Corporation immediately of any proposed changes in staff.

For each proposed staff change, the Contractor must provide the Corporation with a summary of experience of the proposed substitute and an opportunity to interview that person before approval is given or withheld.

The Contractor represents and agrees that its members, officers, employees, agents, servants, consultants, shareholders and subcontractors possess the experience, knowledge and character necessary to qualify them individually for the duties performed under the agreement.
The agreement resulting from this RFP may not be assigned, conveyed, transferred or disposed of by the Contractor.
The Contractor must not subcontract any of its services unless the subcontracting is indicated in its proposal or the State Project Manager gives prior written approval.

All employees of the Contractor or its subcontractors performing Services under the contract must possess the qualifications, training, licenses, and permits required in the jurisdiction where the Services are performed.
All employees of the Contractor or its subcontractors performing Services under the contract must be legally entitled to work in the jurisdiction where the Services are performed.
All persons, corporations, or other legal entities performing Services on behalf of the Contractor must comply with all applicable Federal and State laws concerning employment in the United States.
The respondent must attest that it has read, understood and will comply with the ESD Conflict of Interest Attestation provisions.

The respondent must not offer any gift, in any form, to any ESD employee, member or director during the procurement or contract negotiation where it could be inferred the offer was intended to influence official duty or reward official action.

The respondent may not make offers of employment or discuss possible offers with any ESD employee, member or director involved in this procurement or resulting contract negotiation within at least 30 days from the time that employee's involvement in the matter closed.

The respondent must disclose any existing or contemplated relationship with any other person or entity, including relationships with any member, 5% or greater shareholder, parent, subsidiary or affiliated firm, that would constitute an actual or potential conflict of interest or appearance of impropriety in connection with its rendering of services.
If a conflict of interest does or might exist, the Respondent must describe how it would eliminate or prevent it.

The Respondent must disclose whether it, or any of its members, shareholders of 5% or more, parents, affiliates, or subsidiaries, have been the subject of any ongoing investigation or disciplinary action by the New York State Commission on Ethics and Lobbying in Government or its predecessor State entities.

Where the Respondent or its related entities have been subject to a Commission investigation or disciplinary action, the disclosure must include a description indicating how the matter was resolved or whether it remains unresolved.
Respondents must submit the Offeror Disclosure of Prior Non-Responsibility Determinations as part of their submittal.

The Offeror Disclosure of Prior Non-Responsibility Determinations and the Offeror's Affirmation of Understanding and Agreement forms must be periodically updated during the term of any contract resulting from this RFP.
Respondents are solely responsible for full compliance with the Procurement Requirements under State Finance Law Sections 139-j and 139-k.
The Respondent must have the requisite financial ability, organizational capacity and legal authority to carry out its obligations under this RFP.
The Respondent must demonstrate that both the Respondent and its principals have and will maintain the level of integrity needed to contract with New York State entities such as ESD.
The Respondent must show satisfactory performance of all prior government contracts.
All Respondents must register in the State's Vendor Responsibility System (Vend-Rep System).
The proposal must include a copy of the Respondent's Vend-Rep submission receipt or paper questionnaire.
The Vendor Responsibility Questionnaire must have been completed within one year of submission of the proposal.

All bidders must certify compliance with the New York State Human Rights Law, which prohibits discrimination and harassment based on a protected class and requires reasonable accommodation for persons with disability or pregnancy related conditions.

The Contractor must document its good faith efforts to provide meaningful participation by New York State-certified Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs) as subcontractors and suppliers in performing the Contract.
ESD sets an overall goal of 30 percent MWBE participation for this solicitation.
By submitting a response, the Respondent agrees that ESD may withhold payment under any resulting Contract pending receipt of the required MWBE documentation.
Only sums paid to MWBEs for the performance of a commercially useful function, as defined in 5 NYCRR § 140.1, may be counted toward the MWBE participation goal.

For contracts other than construction contracts, the portion of a contract with an MWBE serving as a broker deemed to represent the commercially useful function is 25 percent of the total contract value.

The Respondent acknowledges that a finding of willful and intentional failure to comply with the MWBE participation goals in a resulting Contract constitutes a breach of contract and allows ESD to withhold payment as liquidated damages.

Liquidated damages shall equal the difference between all sums identified for payment to MWBEs had the Contractor achieved the contractual MWBE goals and all sums actually paid to MWBEs for work performed or materials supplied under the Contract.

By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to demonstrate good faith efforts to achieve the applicable MWBE participation goals by submitting evidence through the New York State Contract System (NYSCS).
A Respondent may arrange to provide the MWBE good faith effort evidence via a non-electronic method by contacting the Office of Contractor and Supplier Diversity (OCSD) at OCSD@esd.ny.gov.
The Respondent must submit an MWBE Utilization Plan with its proposal.
If ESD issues a notice of deficiency on the MWBE Utilization Plan, the Respondent must respond within seven (7) business days of receipt by submitting a written remedy to OCSD at OCSD@esd.ny.gov.

If the written remedy is not timely or is found inadequate by ESD, the Respondent must submit a request for a partial or total waiver of MWBE participation goals within five (5) business days of ESD's direction.

The Respondent's proposal may be disqualified as non-responsive if it fails to submit an MWBE Utilization Plan, a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, a request for waiver, or documentation of good faith efforts.

Any request for a partial or total waiver of established MWBE goal requirements made after Contract Award must be submitted to ESD no later than prior to the submission of a request for final payment on the Contract.

The successful Respondent must submit a quarterly MWBE Contractor Compliance & Payment Report to ESD by the 10th day following each end of quarter over the term of the Contract, documenting progress toward the MWBE goals.
By submitting a proposal, the Respondent agrees to all terms and conditions of SCHEDULE B - PARTICIPATION BY MINORITY AND WOMEN-OWNED BUSINESS ENTERPRISES: REQUIREMENTS AND PROCEDURES.

The Respondent must ensure that it and any subcontractors awarded a subcontract for the construction, demolition, replacement, major repair, renovation, planning or design of real property and improvements thereon undertake or continue programs ensuring minority group members and women are afforded equal employment opportunities without discrimination.
If awarded a Contract, the Respondent must submit a Workforce Utilization Report on a quarterly basis during the term of the Contract in the format required by ESD.
The Respondent must require each of its Subcontractors to submit a Workforce Utilization Report on a quarterly basis during the term of the Contract in the format required by ESD.

Pursuant to Executive Order #162, contractors and subcontractors must report the gross wages paid to each employee for work performed on the contract using the Workforce Utilization Report on a quarterly basis.

The contractor and its subcontractors must not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, creed (religion), color, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, military status, age, disability, predisposing genetic characteristic, marital status or domestic violence victim status.
The contractor must follow the Human Rights Law requirements regarding non-discrimination on the basis of prior criminal conviction and prior arrest.

Respondents are expected to consider New York State certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Businesses (SDVOBs) in fulfilling the requirements of the Contract, whether as subcontractors, suppliers, protégés, or in other partnering or supporting roles.
The Respondent/Contractor should reference the directory of New York State Certified SDVOBs at https://online.ogs.ny.gov/SDVOB/search when providing SDVOB participation.
The Contractor must document "good faith efforts" to provide meaningful participation by SDVOBs as subcontractors or suppliers in the performance of the Contract.
Respondents must submit a completed SDVOB Utilization Plan on Form OCSD-4 in accordance with 9 NYCRR § 252.2(i).

The SDVOB Utilization Plan must list the SDVOBs the Respondent intends to use to perform the Contract, a description of the work each SDVOB will perform to meet the Contract goals, and the estimated dollar amounts to be paid to each SDVOB or, if not known, an estimate of the percentage of Contract work the SDVOB will perform.
Any modifications or changes to the agreed SDVOB participation after Contract award and during the Contract term must be reported on a revised SDVOB Utilization Plan submitted to ESD.
The Respondent must submit a written remedy to a notice of deficiency, as failure to do so may render the proposal non-responsive and subject to disqualification.
The Respondent must document its good faith efforts, as ESD may disqualify the proposal if it determines such efforts were not documented.
Failure to use SDVOBs as agreed in the Utilization Plan constitutes a material breach of the Contract, entitling ESD to remedies including a finding of Contractor non-responsibility.
Before submitting a request for a partial or total waiver of the MWBE/SDVOB goal requirements, the Respondent/Contractor must speak with the Designated Contacts at ESD for guidance.
A Respondent/Contractor that can document good faith efforts to meet the goal requirements may submit a request for a partial or total waiver on Form OCSD-5 accompanied by supporting documentation.
A Respondent may submit its waiver request at the same time it submits its SDVOB Utilization Plan.
The Contractor must attempt in good faith to utilize the SDVOBs identified in its SDVOB Utilization Plan during performance of the Contract.
Waiver requests should be sent to OCSD.
Evidence of required good faith efforts must include copies of solicitations to SDVOBs and any responses thereto.
Evidence of required good faith efforts must include an explanation of the specific reasons each SDVOB that responded to the Respondent/Contractor's solicitation was not selected.

Evidence of required good faith efforts must include the dates of any pre-proposal, pre-award or other meetings attended by the Contractor that were scheduled by ESD with certified SDVOBs ESD determined capable of fulfilling the SDVOB goals set in the Contract.

Evidence of required good faith efforts must include information describing the specific steps undertaken to reasonably structure the Contract scope of work for the purpose of subcontracting with, or obtaining supplies from, certified SDVOBs.
Evidence of required good faith efforts must include any other information deemed relevant to the waiver request.
The Contractor must report Monthly SDVOB Contractor Compliance to ESD during the term of the Contract for the preceding month's activity, documenting progress toward the Contract SDVOB goals.

The Contractor must meet the SDVOB participation goals set forth in the Contract, and willful and intentional failure to comply constitutes breach of contract with damages payable as set forth therein.
The Respondent is strongly encouraged and expected to consider New York State businesses in fulfilling the requirements of the contract.
Each Respondent must complete the Encouraging Use of New York State Businesses in Contract Performance form as part of its Proposal.
Only the prime consultant needs to complete Form ST 220-CA, but Schedule A to Form ST 220-TD requires detailed information from the sub-consultants, such as tax ID number, if applicable.
If applicable, certificates of authority must be attached by the prime consultant and all the subconsultants.
Any contract resulting from this solicitation will require periodic updating of the certifications contained in Form ST-220-CA.
Respondents must not include the information or documentation required by Schedule A in their proposal submission, aside from information otherwise required by this solicitation.
Respondents must review the terms of Schedule A and submit any concerns in writing together with the Respondent's Administrative Proposal.
Successful Respondents will be required to accept the terms of Schedule A as part of the executed contract.
The selected Respondent must provide Commercial General Liability insurance of $1 million per occurrence and $2 million in the aggregate.
If the Respondent uses a vehicle in business, it must carry Commercial Automobile insurance with a limit of not less than $1 million.
The selected Respondent must provide Sexual Abuse and Molestation Insurance of $1 million.
The selected Respondent must show evidence of Worker's Compensation and Employer's Liability insurance at State statutory limits.
The selected Respondent must show evidence of Disability insurance coverage at State statutory limits.

NYS Urban Development Corporation d/b/a Empire State Development (ESD) must be named as additional insured on a primary and non-contributory basis on the Commercial General Liability and Auto Liability policies.
All required insurance policies must include a waiver of subrogation in favor of ESD.
An unsuccessful Respondent must request a debriefing within 15 calendar days of ESD's notification that its proposal was not selected for award.

component_records.title: Program management office and ESD governance
component_records.description: A dedicated PMO led by a named Program Director runs the engagement: a monthly timeline from award through first-cohort internship or job completion, a single point of contact for ESD, monthly status and data reporting, and a change-control log. The PMO holds the contract term of up to 18 months with renewal or extension options, and manages the schedule against the January 1, 2026 start and the November 14, 2025 award announcement. It also owns the restricted-period protocol, routing all procurement contact through the designated ESD contacts by email only.

component_records.title: Track A and Track B program design and combined-bid capacity plan
component_records.description: We deliver a single program architecture with two configured tracks: Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) for low-income matriculating undergraduates, and Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs) as an accelerated bootcamp alternative to a degree for low-income New Yorkers facing barriers to employment. The design specifies cohort size, training duration, part-time and full-time immersive schedules, stipend levels, credential outcomes, and the academic-year versus summer calendar aligned to employer internship hiring cycles. A written capacity and strategy plan shows how one organization runs both tracks simultaneously with separate cohort calendars, shared services and distinct success-coach ratios.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment and eligibility screening
component_records.description: A targeted recruitment engine reaches low-income New Yorkers underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own: campus partnerships with New York colleges and universities, community-based organization referrals, and outreach to workforce and re-entry networks for Track B. The application and evaluation process uses a scored rubric, documented eligibility verification against the Pell-based low-income definition, and a needs assessment at intake that records each barrier (childcare, transportation, device and connectivity, work schedule) and the support assigned to it. Recruitment targets are set per cohort to reach the 250-participant floor and the 400-participant priority tier.

component_records.title: Industry-informed AI curriculum and instruction
component_records.description: An online AI curriculum built with named leading researchers and industry experts, covering applied machine learning, data engineering, model evaluation and responsible AI, with real-world machine learning projects drawn from employer partners. Each module carries defined learning outcomes and assessment instruments so skill attainment is measured during training, not only at completion. A curriculum council of employer partners and academic advisors meets quarterly to retire stale content and add emerging topics, and the curriculum is version-controlled so ESD can see what changed and why.

component_records.title: Participant supports: stipends, mentors, coaches and professional development
component_records.description: Every participant receives a stipend at the level stated in the budget, plus wraparound supports: a matched industry mentor, a career coach with AI hiring experience, and professional development covering interview practice, portfolio and GitHub presentation, and workplace norms. Success coaches run scheduled check-ins and an early-warning dashboard on attendance and assessment scores, triggering intervention before a participant drops. Track B participants receive additional barrier-specific supports identified in the needs assessment.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships and placement services
component_records.description: An employer partnerships group recruits and stewards leading New York tech companies, securing written commitment letters for paid internships (Track A) and full-time AI roles (Track B) before the first cohort completes. The group runs an employer advisory council that feeds hiring requirements into the curriculum, hosts a candidate-matching process with employer interviews, and tracks placement rates by track and by low-income status. Placement support continues after program completion until the participant is placed or the coaching window closes.

component_records.title: Data, performance measurement and ESD reporting
component_records.description: A participant data system captures the full ESD data set: applicant counts and low-income percentage, enrollment counts and low-income percentage, completion counts and low-income percentage, paid internship placement rate and low-income share, full-time placement rate and low-income share, participating colleges and universities, and participating employer partners. Data is available to ESD on request and delivered in a standard monthly report plus a quarterly performance review against the 250-participant floor, the 50% low-income threshold and the majority-placement target. The system is built to accept additional data points ESD fixes at contract negotiation without re-platforming.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
component_records.description: A line-by-line price proposal maps personnel services (job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percent of time, cost to contract) and other-than-personnel-services costs (each on its own line with unit count and cost to contract) across the full program period. The budget stays within $2M for one track and $4M for both, excludes all indirect costs, and states the extent of any cost match in the ESD budget template. A written justification ties each cost line to a program activity and to the participant volumes it supports.

component_records.title: Compliance, contract and insurance obligations
component_records.description: A compliance function carries every non-technical obligation in the contract: Schedule A acceptance and concerns raised in writing with the Administrative Proposal, OSC review and approval before the contract is enforceable, professional-standards warranty and free correction of patent errors, 30-day change-order claims with continued performance, ESD approval of staff and substitutes, no assignment, subcontractor disclosure and prior written approval, and employment-law compliance for all staff. It also maintains the insurance program (CGL $1M/$2M, Commercial Auto $1M, Sexual Abuse and Molestation $1M, statutory Workers' Compensation, Disability and Employer's Liability, ESD as additional insured, waiver of subrogation), the conflict-of-interest and gift/employment restrictions, the 139-j/139-k and ST-220-CA certifications, Vend-Rep registration, and the Human Rights Law and non-discrimination certifications.
